transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess what finally made me make the appointment is I keep forgetting these small things that I usually handle without thinking. Like returning phone calls, or I had this registration form I was supposed to turn in and it just sat there, and then I’ll mean to stop somewhere on the way home for an errand and completely pass it.

It sounds minor when I say it out loud, but it’s been happening enough that it’s starting to bother me. I’m a secretary, so I’m used to keeping track of things for other people, and then I get home and realize I forgot something really basic. That’s kind of what pushed me to come in.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking or memory besides forgetting small tasks? For example, confusion, getting lost in familiar places, or trouble finding the right words?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like getting lost or being confused, no. I mean, sometimes I walk into a room and forget why I went in there, but I feel like everybody does that, right?

Trouble finding words… not really. I might blank for a second if I’m distracted, but I wouldn’t say it’s like I can’t remember names of things or anything. It’s more just… I have a thought, and then something else happens, like the phone rings or I see dishes in the sink, and then I’m off doing that instead. Actually my kitchen counter is kind of the worst for that, because I put papers there and then they just disappear under other papers… but no, not confusion or getting lost.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling more down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling more irritable than usual?

Um… mood? I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I get annoyed with myself when I forget something, like I’ll be looking for a paper and then I find three other things I meant to deal with, and then I’m mad because now the counter is a mess again.

But I wouldn’t say I’m, like, more down than usual or not enjoying things. I still like my usual stuff when I actually sit down to do it. It’s more… frustration, I guess, because I feel scattered. But I don’t know if that counts as a mood change.

Do you find it harder than before to stay focused on tasks, even when you're not interrupted? Like reading a few paragraphs and realizing you don't remember what you just read, or having your mind wander a lot during routine activities?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not always that I’m interrupted, exactly… sometimes it’s just one little thing. Like at work, if the phone rings, or someone nearby is talking, I’ll look up and then completely lose where I was in whatever I was doing.

Or even I’ll be sitting there and suddenly remember something at home, like “oh, did I move the laundry?”—well, not that it matters right then, but then my brain is over there instead of on the form or email in front of me. And then I have to kind of restart what I was doing. It’s frustrating because the office isn’t even that chaotic, it’s just normal office noise, but it pulls me off track.
Do you also find it hard to stay focused or keep things organized during your personal time, like when you're at home or doing something for yourself?

Yeah… at home it definitely shows up more, I think. I can usually keep it together at work, mostly because there’s a structure there and people are expecting things, but since I started taking evening classes, it’s like all the loose ends have multiplied.

My desk at home turns into piles, and then my class folder is supposed to be organized, but somehow papers just get shoved in there. And I’ll set email reminders for myself, but then there are so many that I spend time just figuring out what I’m supposed to do first instead of actually doing it.

It’s not like I’m doing nothing, exactly. I’m busy the whole time, but I’ll look up and realize I’ve been sorting papers or checking reminders and I still haven’t started the assignment I sat down to do. Then I get annoyed because I only have so much time in the evening.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level lately, like feeling more tired than usual even after rest or finding it hard to get started on tasks?

I don’t know if it’s energy exactly… like I’m not falling asleep or anything. It’s more getting started, especially if I know something is going to take a lot of sitting and thinking.

Like for class, if I have to read a long chapter or write out a plan for an assignment, I’ll keep finding other things to do first. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to clear off the table, or check one email, and then somehow it’s late. Then after work I’m rushing through it, which is… not great. I guess it feels tiring before I even start, if that makes sense.

Can you describe what happens when you're trying to start a task you know you need to do—like your class assignment—do you feel overwhelmed by how to begin, or do you just keep shifting to other things without really knowing why?

Yeah, it’s more like I keep shifting to other things. I mean, sometimes I do feel like I don’t know where to start, but mostly if it’s something like a long chapter or I have to write out a plan, I just… don’t sit down and do it.

I’ll suddenly decide I should clean up my bag, or check something for tomorrow, or make tea—and then I get kind of involved in that. Then it’s late, and I’m doing the assignment after work when I’m already kind of rushed. It’s not even that I meant to avoid it, exactly, but that’s what happens.
Do you find it hard to get started on tasks even when you know exactly what you need to do and there’s nothing else distracting you?

Yeah, I mean… even if I know what it is, like “read this chapter” or “write the plan,” I still keep putting it off. It’s not always because something is distracting me right then. I’ll just kind of not start.

Like I’ll sit there with the book nearby, and then I’m thinking I should maybe get a drink first, or check if I printed the right thing, and then—sorry, this is probably the same thing I said before—but it ends up being late. Then after work I’m rushing through it, and I’m irritated because I did know what I needed to do. It just felt like I couldn’t make myself sit down and do that long, thinking kind of task.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble staying focused or keeping things organized even as a child, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. Like even in elementary school I was always the kid who forgot the permission slip or had the homework but couldn’t find it because it was somewhere in my backpack.

My mom used to have to kind of walk me through projects step by step, and teachers would remind me what to do next. I remember one time with a poster project—well, I don’t remember what the project was even about—but I remember everyone else seemed to just know how to get it done, and I needed someone to keep telling me, “Okay, now do this part.” So no, I don’t think it’s just recent.
Would you say these issues with focus and staying on task have always been mild, or have they sometimes caused bigger problems—like affecting your grades, work performance, or relationships?

I’d say it’s mostly been mild, like I’m not completely falling apart or anything. I’m still getting by.

But it has caused problems in smaller ways that kind of add up. At work I’ve missed little follow-ups—like someone asks me to check back on something and I’ll mean to, and then it slips. Not huge disasters, but enough that I worry people notice. And with school stuff, I’ve missed deadlines or turned things in late more than I’d like.

I guess what bothers me is I’m trying to be seen as reliable, especially because I’d like to maybe move into an Office Manager role eventually, and I worry this makes me look scattered or like I’m not ready for that.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or keeping things organized in other situations, like when you're out with friends or in public places?

Yeah, somewhat. I notice it more at the office or in class-type situations, honestly. Like if a phone rings, or two people start talking nearby, I’m suddenly listening to that instead of what I was doing.

And sometimes it’s not even something outside—like I’ll randomly think, “Oh, did I pay that bill?” or something about home, and then I’ve lost the thread. Sorry, I know you asked about friends and public places… I guess in public it can happen too, but the clearest examples for me are work or sitting in a class where I’m supposed to stay on one thing.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have a hard time staying seated, especially when you're trying to focus on something?

Yeah, a little. I wouldn’t say I’m like getting up and pacing around all the time, but in longer classes especially I notice I’m doing things like clicking my pen or bouncing my foot. Or I keep shifting around in the chair even though I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.

It’s funny, I’ll sometimes only realize because someone looks over, and then I’m like, oh, I’m doing that again. But yeah, mostly when I have to sit there for a while.
Do you also notice these issues with staying focused or getting started on tasks when you're in more relaxed or social situations, like hanging out with friends or watching a movie at home?

Yeah, I mean… at home or with friends it’s less obvious, I guess because there’s not always one specific thing I’m supposed to be doing. Like with a movie, sometimes I’ll drift, but the bigger thing I notice is really at the office or in class.

Like one phone rings, or people start talking nearby, and suddenly I’m listening to that instead of whatever I was working on. Or I’ll be in the middle of something and randomly think about something at home, and then I’ve kind of lost where I was. So… socially, maybe a little, but the clearest place it happens is when I’m supposed to stay focused on a task.
